name: FATF 40 Recommendations on Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing

articles.title: Assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach
articles.requirement: Countries must identify, assess, and understand their ML/TF risks and apply a risk-based approach to ensure measures are commensurate with the risks identified.

articles.title: National cooperation and coordination
articles.requirement: Countries should have national AML/CFT policies informed by risks identified, and designate an authority for coordination of policy and operational cooperation.

articles.title: Money laundering offence
articles.requirement: Countries should criminalise money laundering on the basis of the Vienna Convention and the Palermo Convention, applying it to all serious offences with a view to including the widest range of predicate offences.

articles.title: Confiscation and provisional measures
articles.requirement: Countries should adopt measures to enable confiscation of laundered property, proceeds, instrumentalities, and property of corresponding value, and provisional measures such as freezing and seizing.

articles.title: Terrorist financing offence
articles.requirement: Countries should criminalise terrorist financing on the basis of the Terrorist Financing Convention, covering financing of terrorist acts, terrorist organisations, and individual terrorists.

articles.title: Targeted financial sanctions — terrorism
articles.requirement: Countries should implement targeted financial sanctions regimes to comply with UN Security Council resolutions relating to terrorism and terrorist financing, including freezing without delay.

articles.title: Targeted financial sanctions — proliferation
articles.requirement: Countries should implement targeted financial sanctions to comply with UN Security Council resolutions relating to the prevention, suppression, and disruption of proliferation of WMDs and financing thereof.

articles.title: Non-profit organisations
articles.requirement: Countries should review the adequacy of laws and regulations relating to NPOs to prevent their misuse for terrorist financing, using a risk-based approach.

articles.title: Financial institution secrecy laws
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure that financial institution secrecy laws do not inhibit implementation of the FATF Recommendations.

articles.title: Customer due diligence
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should identify and verify the identity of customers, beneficial owners, and understand the nature of the business relationship. Ongoing due diligence is required.

articles.title: Record keeping
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should maintain all necessary records on transactions and CDD information for at least five years, available to competent authorities.

articles.title: Politically exposed persons
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should have risk management systems to determine if a customer or beneficial owner is a PEP, and apply enhanced due diligence measures for foreign PEPs and domestic PEPs where higher risk.

articles.title: Correspondent banking
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should assess the respondent institution's AML/CFT controls, obtain senior management approval, and clearly understand the respective responsibilities.

articles.title: Money or value transfer services
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure MVTS providers are licensed or registered and subject to effective AML/CFT regulation and supervision. Agents must be included in AML/CFT programmes.

articles.title: New technologies and virtual assets
articles.requirement: Countries should identify and assess ML/TF risks of new technologies including virtual assets. VASPs should be licensed/registered, supervised, and subject to FATF Recommendations (including travel rule).

articles.title: Wire transfers (Travel Rule)
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure originator and beneficiary information accompanies wire transfers and that financial institutions monitor transfers lacking required information.

articles.title: Reliance on third parties
articles.requirement: Countries may permit financial institutions to rely on third parties to perform CDD, provided the institution obtains necessary information immediately, and the third party is regulated and supervised.

articles.title: Internal controls and foreign branches and subsidiaries
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should implement AML/CFT programmes including compliance management, employee screening, training, and an independent audit function. Programmes must be applied to foreign branches and subsidiaries.

articles.title: Higher-risk countries
articles.requirement: Financial institutions should apply enhanced due diligence measures to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons from countries identified by FATF as higher risk.

articles.title: Reporting of suspicious transactions
articles.requirement: If a financial institution suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect funds are proceeds of crime or related to terrorist financing, it must report promptly to the FIU.

articles.title: Tipping-off and confidentiality
articles.requirement: Financial institutions, their directors, officers, and employees should be protected from criminal and civil liability for STR filing in good faith, and prohibited from disclosing that an STR has been filed.

articles.title: DNFBPs — Customer due diligence
articles.requirement: Designated non-financial businesses and professions (casinos, real estate, dealers in precious metals/stones, lawyers, notaries, accountants, TCSPs) must apply CDD requirements.

articles.title: DNFBPs — Other measures
articles.requirement: DNFBPs should apply record keeping, PEP, new technology, higher-risk country, and reporting requirements as set out in Recommendations 11, 12, 15, 19, 20, and 21.

articles.title: Transparency and BO of legal persons
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure adequate, accurate, and timely information on beneficial ownership of legal persons is obtainable or accessible by competent authorities, using a multi-pronged approach.

articles.title: Transparency and BO of legal arrangements
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure adequate, accurate, and timely information on express trusts and similar legal arrangements (trustees, settlors, beneficiaries) is available to competent authorities.

articles.title: Regulation and supervision of financial institutions
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure financial institutions are subject to adequate AML/CFT regulation and supervision, with supervisors having adequate powers and resources to monitor and enforce compliance.

articles.title: Powers of supervisors
articles.requirement: Supervisors should have adequate powers to supervise or monitor and ensure compliance, including the power to compel production of information, conduct inspections, and apply sanctions.

articles.title: Regulation and supervision of DNFBPs
articles.requirement: DNFBPs should be subject to regulatory and supervisory measures as set out in Recommendation 26, with designated competent authorities having adequate powers.

articles.title: Financial intelligence units
articles.requirement: Countries should establish an FIU that serves as a national centre for receiving, analysing, and disseminating STRs and other ML/TF-relevant information.

articles.title: Responsibilities of law enforcement
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure designated law enforcement authorities have responsibility for ML/TF investigations and should conduct proactive parallel financial investigations alongside predicate offences.

articles.title: Powers of law enforcement and investigative authorities
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure investigators can use a wide range of investigative techniques including undercover operations, intercepting communications, accessing computer systems, and controlled delivery.

articles.title: Cash couriers
articles.requirement: Countries should have measures to detect physical cross-border transportation of currency and bearer negotiable instruments, including a declaration/disclosure system.

articles.title: Statistics
articles.requirement: Countries should maintain comprehensive statistics on matters relevant to the effectiveness of their AML/CFT systems, including STRs filed, investigations, prosecutions, convictions, and assets frozen/confiscated.

articles.title: Guidance and feedback
articles.requirement: Competent authorities and SRBs should establish guidelines and provide feedback to assist financial institutions and DNFBPs in applying AML/CFT measures, particularly in detecting and reporting suspicious transactions.

articles.title: Sanctions
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure effective, proportionate, and dissuasive sanctions (criminal, civil, or administrative) are available for natural and legal persons that fail to comply with AML/CFT requirements.

articles.title: International instruments
articles.requirement: Countries should become party to and implement fully the Vienna Convention, Palermo Convention, Terrorist Financing Convention, and Merida Convention.

articles.title: Mutual legal assistance
articles.requirement: Countries should rapidly provide the widest possible range of mutual legal assistance in relation to ML/TF investigations, prosecutions, and related proceedings.

articles.title: Mutual legal assistance — freezing and confiscation
articles.requirement: Countries should have authority to take expeditious action in response to foreign requests to identify, freeze, seize, and confiscate laundered property and proceeds.

articles.title: Extradition
articles.requirement: Countries should constructively and effectively execute extradition requests relating to ML and TF without undue delay, or prosecute at home where extradition is refused.

articles.title: Other forms of international cooperation
articles.requirement: Countries should ensure their competent authorities can rapidly provide international cooperation to foreign counterparts, including spontaneous exchange, for AML/CFT purposes.
